title: The Last Prom
premise: Theo Sandoval has spent senior year being invisible—raising two younger siblings while their mom works hospital night shifts, keeping grades up and attention down. But when Ms. Okafor pairs Theo with Priya Chandrasekaran, the student council president and Theo's longtime rival, for a semester project on 'community power structures,' the pair accidentally uncovers that the school's beloved prom committee is a rigged machine: Principal Voss and boosters have been funneling prom funds into an elite scholarship program reserved for insider families. To expose it, Theo and Priya must enter—and win—the very popularity contest they despise: running for prom king and queen as a protest ticket. The campaign costs Theo his invisibility, nearly his family's stability, and his fragile alliance with Priya, but at prom itself they trigger the reveal that forces Voss's resignation and wins real scholarships for overlooked students like Theo.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former night-shift barista who wrote her first novel in the margins of receipt paper while putting herself through community college. She writes stories about kids who hold families together and still find room to want something of their own.

chapters.title: Head Down
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A pre-dawn montage: packing lunches for Mateo and Luz, covering mom's missed parent-teacher call, acing a quiz no one notices. Establishes Theo's rules of invisibility and the quiet pride in holding the family together. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ms. Okafor announces semester partners for the civics capstone: 'Sandoval and Chandrasekaran.' Priya, polished and furious, assumes Theo will drag her grade down; Theo assumes she'll report them for missing study sessions. They agree to minimal contact. Beat: mutual contempt masking curiosity.

chapters.title: Prom Is Coming
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Inside the student council machine: budget spreadsheets, Voss's charm offensive, the boosters' private dinner. Priya notices a $12,000 discrepancy labeled 'venue upgrades' for a venue already booked free. She pockets the page. Beat: first crack in her loyalty.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Forced library session devolves into a fight about who works harder to be liked. Theo lets slip nothing personal; Priya clocks the lunch receipts in Theo's backpack and says nothing. Truce: divide the research, never talk about home. Beat: grudging respect seeded.

chapters.title: Luz's Field Trip Form
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mom's shift runs long; Theo misses turning in Luz's permission slip and gets a truancy warning letter addressed to the household head. Panic about foster-adjacent scrutiny. Priya witnesses the meltdown outside the office and covers by claiming Theo as her project partner meeting. Beat: the mask slips once.

chapters.title: Follow the Money
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. The pair traces the discrepancy: the 'Rosewood Scholars Fund' awards go exclusively to booster families' kids—including Priya's best friend Dana. Priya wants to believe it's coincidence. Theo recognizes the shape of systems built to exclude. Beat: shared outrage begins.

chapters.title: Dana
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Dana gently; Dana admits she knew, justifies it ('my parents earned this'), and warns Priya that Voss protects his own. Their friendship fractures. Priya realizes she's been the acceptable face of an unfair machine. Beat: identity crisis.

chapters.title: The Idea That Ruins Everything
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. For the capstone, Theo proposes a live case study: run for prom court on a reform ticket and document how power responds. Priya calls it career suicide—she needs the council's recommendation letter. But she can't unsee the numbers. Beat: reckless hope vs. ambition.

chapters.title: Petition Signatures
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They collect signatures among the invisible kids: cafeteria workers' children, ESL students, band kids. Mateo helps design posters; Luz becomes their tiny hype squad. The campaign feels like family extended outward. Beat: belonging, newly defined.

chapters.title: Voss Invites Them to Tea
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Voss offers Priya a guaranteed Rosewood Scholarship if she withdraws. He speaks warmly about her future, coldly about Theo's 'circumstances.' Priya keeps smiling and records nothing—but remembers everything. Beat: corruption wears a kind face.

chapters.title: Home Invasion (of Time)
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Campaigning eats caregiving hours; Mateo skips homework, Luz cries at pickup, and mom, exhausted, asks if Theo is trying to get them noticed by the wrong people. Theo snaps that everything is always about staying small. Beat: the cost of wanting more.

chapters.title: Debate Night Sabotage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the candidate forum, opponents mock Theo's 'no parental involvement' and someone leaks that Theo is effectively the household guardian. Instead of shame, Theo tells the truth plainly—and the room goes silent, then loud. Beat: invisibility weaponized into honesty.

chapters.title: The Middle Chapter Fight
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Theo planned to drop out of the race to protect the siblings after an anonymous threat about custody. She's furious—Theo decided for both of them, again alone. She demands partnership or nothing. Beat: alliance breaks over trust, not tactics.

chapters.title: Alone, Loudly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Campaigning solo goes badly; a smear flyer circulates with Luz's photo. Mom comes home early, sees the flyer, and instead of anger shows Theo her own old rejection letters from nursing school. 'They counted us out too.' Beat: generational solidarity.

chapters.title: Priya's Letter
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya receives her early-decision acceptance contingent on the council letter—which Voss controls. She burns the draft withdrawal speech, walks into his office, and tells him she'll testify anyway. Beat: choosing integrity over the golden path.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Copy Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo finds Priya photocopying evidence at midnight. Apologies without excuses; they merge their findings into one timeline. Mateo delivers snacks and declares himself campaign manager. Beat: the team reforms, stronger and honest.

chapters.title: Election Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Voting is close; Voss delays results citing 'irregularities,' then announces the rival ticket won amid suspicious tallies. The gym erupts in protest. Theo and Priya refuse to concede and announce they'll speak at prom regardless. Beat: injustice sharpened to a point.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Quiet interlude before prom: sewing a thrifted suit, Luz's glitter everywhere, mom working a double but leaving a note: 'Make noise.' Theo realizes the championship that mattered was never the crown. Beat: calm before the storm.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The gym is transformed; Voss crowns the rival ticket early to cut speeches short. As the lights dim for the dance, Theo takes the mic during the playlist 'malfunction' Mateo engineered. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Reveal
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya presents the fund trail on the projector while Theo names every student the Rosewood money skipped. Teachers who suspected come forward; a booster defects on the spot. Students link arms rather than let the mic be cut. Beat: collective power, climax.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. District investigation; Voss resigns; the fund is restructured with open applications. Theo doesn't win prom king—the rival ticket does—but the new principal announces need-blind scholarships from the recovered funds, and Theo's name is first on the list. Beat: justice without fairy tale.

chapters.title: The Last Slow Song
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing scene. On the gym floor, Theo and Priya—friends now, something maybe more later—dance badly while Luz and Mateo wave from the bleachers. Theo submits the capstone titled 'Who Gets to Be Seen.' Final line: visibility was never the prize; belonging was. Beat: warm, earned resolution.
